root.label: Strict weak ordering
root.note: The shape every library comparator must have: a ranking with ties.

children.label: The four laws
children.note: Required by [alg.sorting.general] for sorting and ordered containers.

children.label: Irreflexive
children.note: comp(a, a) is false: nothing comes before itself.

children.label: Asymmetric
children.note: If comp(a, b) then not comp(b, a).

children.label: Transitive
children.note: comp(a, b) and comp(b, c) imply comp(a, c).

children.label: Incomparability transitive
children.note: Ties chain: equiv(a, b) and equiv(b, c) imply equiv(a, c); this makes it weak, not partial.

children.label: Equivalence
children.note: equiv(a, b) is !comp(a, b) && !comp(b, a); operator== is never consulted.

children.label: Set lookup
children.note: find, count and contains locate equivalent keys; a case-insensitive set rejects "APPLE" after "Apple".

children.label: ranges::find differs
children.note: Generic searches use ==, so they can disagree with the container's own lookup.

children.label: min, max, merge
children.note: On equivalent arguments min and max return the first; merge takes from the first range first.

children.label: Broken comparators
children.note: Violating the laws is undefined behavior, not an odd but valid order.

children.label: <= or >=
children.note: Breaks irreflexivity; libstdc++ sort can read out of bounds on long runs of equal values.

children.label: NaN with <
children.note: NaN ties with everything, so incomparability is not transitive.

children.label: OR of two keys
children.note: Breaks asymmetry: (1,2) and (2,1) each come before the other.

children.label: Debug checking
children.note: -D_GLIBCXX_DEBUG checks irreflexivity in std::sort; release builds check nothing.

children.label: Writing them right
children.note: Compare the next key only when the previous keys tie.

children.label: std::tie
children.note: tie(a.x, a.y) < tie(b.x, b.y) compares lexicographically; needs lvalues.

children.label: <=> chains
children.note: if (auto c = a.k <=> b.k; c != 0) return c < 0; then the next key.

children.label: strong_order for doubles
children.note: std::strong_order(a, b) < 0 is a total order that also orders NaN and signed zeros.

children.label: sort vs stable_sort
children.note: They differ only in what happens to equivalent elements.

children.label: sort
children.note: O(N log N) comparisons in the worst case since C++11; equivalent order unspecified.

children.label: stable_sort
children.note: Keeps equivalent elements in input order; O(N log^2 N) if no buffer is available.

children.label: Ranges tools
children.note: Constrained algorithms add concepts and projections.

children.label: ranges::less
children.note: Default comparator, constrained by totally_ordered_with; total order over pointers.

children.label: strict_weak_order concept
children.note: Purely syntactic: ranges::less_equal satisfies it.

children.label: Projections
children.note: Applied to elements, not to the searched value; ranges::sort(v, {}, &P::age).
